lessons.title: Working at the stations of the small stock line
lessons.html:
The main work experience

This is the largest work experience module of the Small Stock Slaughterer qualification. Over many weeks you work at each station of a sheep and goat line with a mentor. You must show that you can do each process to the abattoir's standard, safely, hygienically and at line speed.

Stations you will work at

StationMain task
Stunning (when authorised)Make the animal unconscious
Shackling and bleedingHoist and cut the blood vessels
LeggingOpen the skin on the legs, remove feet
Heading and weasandRemove the head, tie the oesophagus
Fisting and skin pullingFree and remove the skin
BungingFree and tie the rectum
EviscerationRemove rough and red offal
Inspection presentationKeep carcass, head and organs matched
Trimming and washingRemove contamination, wash
Weighing and chillingRecord mass, move to chiller

You will usually start at simpler stations and move on when your mentor sees you are ready. Skinning stations take the longest to learn well.

Quality before speed

At first you will be slower than experienced workers. Focus on clean, correct work. If you fall behind, tell your team leader; do not skip steps. One carcass with wool or dung on it can cost more time than slowing the line.

lessons.title: Safe and hygienic work on the line
lessons.html:
Knife skills

  • Keep knives sharp; use the steel often.
  • Cut away from your body and your other hand.
  • Wear the cut-resistant glove and arm or chest protection your plant provides.
  • Never try to catch a falling knife.
  • Carry knives in a scabbard.
  • Use two knives in turn so one is always in the sterilizer.

Hygiene at every station

  • The woolly outside of the skin must never touch the meat.
  • Sterilise your knife after each carcass and after every cut through the skin.
  • Wash your hands after touching wool or the outside of the animal.
  • Keep carcasses off the floor and away from platforms and each other.
  • Report contamination you cannot fix at your station.

Animal welfare on the line

Every animal must be properly stunned before bleeding, and dead before dressing starts. If you see an animal on the line showing signs of life, shout a warning so it is re-stunned at once.

Machines

  • Use only machines you are trained and authorised for.
  • Know the emergency stops.
  • Keep hands away from skin pullers, chains and moving parts.

Your body

Repeated cutting and pulling can strain your wrists, shoulders and back. Use sharp knives, stand at the right height on the platform, and do the stretches your plant teaches. Report pain early.

Injuries

Report every cut or injury to your supervisor and get first aid from a trained first aider. First aid must be learned in hands-on training by an accredited provider.

lessons.title: Assessment and portfolio of evidence
lessons.html:
How you are assessed

Your mentor watches you at each station on several days. For each process the mentor checks that you:

  • Follow the abattoir's procedure in the correct order.
  • Keep wool and dirt off the meat.
  • Work safely and wear your PPE.
  • Sterilise tools and wash hands at the right times.
  • Produce a carcass that meets the standard: clean, no knife scores, no torn fat, no gut contamination.
  • Keep up with the line, or ask for help in time.
  • Follow the meat inspector's instructions.

Your portfolio

  • A daily logbook: station, date, number of carcasses, what went well, what you need to improve.
  • Mentor comments and signatures for each station.
  • Notes on mistakes and how you corrected them. Example: 'Cut the rumen twice on Monday. Mentor showed me to lift the belly wall with two fingers. No gut cuts on Tuesday.'
  • Records of any incidents.

Honesty

Mistakes happen while you learn. Always report them so they can be fixed. Hiding a gut cut, wool on the meat or a dropped carcass puts people at risk and is a serious offence.

At the end

You should be able to work at any station on the small stock line and explain why each step matters. This prepares you for the external assessment of the qualification and for growing into a team leader.

Key points

  • Work at every station of the small stock line under a mentor.
  • Quality comes before speed; never skip steps.
  • Keep wool off the meat and sterilise knives after every carcass.
  • Shout a warning if an animal on the line shows signs of life.
  • Report mistakes and injuries, and keep your portfolio signed and honest.
